source: NCERT Class VIII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Economics Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. What are Factors of Production
points: **Production** = making goods and services to satisfy human wants.
The resources used to produce goods and services are called the **factors of production**.
There are **four factors: Land, Labour, Capital and Entrepreneurship**.

sections.heading: 2. The Four Factors
points: **Land** — all **natural resources** used in production (soil, water, minerals, forests, air).
**Labour** — the **human effort**, physical and mental, used in production.
**Capital** — the **man-made goods** used to produce more goods (tools, machines, buildings, money invested).
**Entrepreneurship (Enterprise)** — the person who **organises** the other three factors, takes **decisions** and bears the **risk** of the business.

sections.heading: 3. Rewards of the Factors
points: **Land → Rent.**
**Labour → Wages/Salary.**
**Capital → Interest.**
**Entrepreneur → Profit** (what remains after paying the other three; may also be a loss).

sections.heading: 4. Combining the Factors
points: Production needs **all four factors together** — none can produce alone.
The **entrepreneur** brings them together in the right proportion.
Improving the **quality** of factors (skilled labour, better capital/technology) raises **productivity**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Four factors of production: Land, Labour, Capital, Entrepreneurship.
Land = natural resources; Labour = human effort; Capital = man-made goods; Entrepreneur = organiser & risk-taker.
Rewards: Land → rent, Labour → wages, Capital → interest, Entrepreneur → profit.
All four factors are needed together to produce.
Better quality factors (skilled labour, technology) raise productivity.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Match rewards: **Land=rent, Labour=wages, Capital=interest, Entrepreneur=profit**.
**Capital = man-made goods used in production** (tools/machines), not natural resources.
**Land** in economics means **all natural resources**, not just soil.
The **entrepreneur** bears the **risk** and earns **profit** (or bears loss).
